Description: The one-dimensional extent of an object or the distance between two points.
A measure of the amount of matter in an object and its resistance to acceleration.
The progression of events from the past through the present into the future.
The rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor.
A measure of the average kinetic energy of particles in a system; absolute temperature.
A measure of the number of specified elementary entities (atoms, molecules, etc.) in a sample.
The power of a light source in a particular direction, weighted by the luminosity function.
The rate of change of position with respect to time; a vector quantity.
The rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
An interaction that causes a change in motion of an object; equal to mass × acceleration (Newton's second law).
The capacity to do work; includes kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, and other forms.
The rate of energy transfer or work done per unit time.
The force applied perpendicular to a surface per unit area.
A fundamental property of matter; the quantity of electricity carried by a particle.
The work done per unit charge to move a charge between two points; electromotive force.
The number of occurrences of a repeating event per unit time.
The angle between two lines or planes, measured in radians; a supplementary quantity.
The two-dimensional angle in three-dimensional space subtended at a point, measured in steradians.
The luminous flux incident per unit area of a surface; how much light falls on a given area.
The magnetic force per unit charge per unit velocity; the density of magnetic flux through a surface. Also called magnetic induction.
The total magnetic field passing through a given surface; the surface integral of the magnetic flux density.
The property of a conductor by which a change in current induces an electromotive force (EMF) in the conductor itself or in a nearby conductor.
The total perceived power of light emitted by a source, weighted by the luminosity function to reflect human eye sensitivity.
The mean energy deposited by ionizing radiation per unit mass of matter; used in radiation physics and dosimetry.
The increase in rate of a chemical reaction caused by a catalyst; the amount of substance converted per unit time.
The absorbed dose weighted by radiation type to reflect biological harm; used in radiological protection. Dimensionally equal to absorbed dose but biologically contextualized.
The ease with which electric current passes through a conductor; the reciprocal of electrical resistance.
The ability of a system to store electric charge per unit electric potential difference.
The opposition that a conductor presents to the flow of electric current for a given potential difference; the reciprocal of electrical conductance.
The number of nuclear decays (disintegrations) occurring in a radioactive sample per unit time; a measure of radioactivity.
